ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r3.claim: She proposed gifts as a diplomatic compromise to test Solomon’s response and avert war; she expected little success because she knew gifts would not sway his ideological principles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r3.anchor: she wanted to gauge the response

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r4.claim: The queen’s plan shows she was a peace-loving ruler with foresight who sought a better outcome for herself and her people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p482/r4.anchor: This shows that she was a peace-loving ruler having insight of the future.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p205/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p205/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p205/r10.claim: A hadiyya is something brought to a person as a gift of honor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p205/r10.anchor: الهدية: ما سيق إلى الإنسان مما يتحف به على سبيل التكرمة.

STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.claim: The account of Solomon's miraculous host and encounter with the Queen of Sheba ends with her embracing faith in the One God.
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.anchor: Solomon with his miraculous host of men, jinn, and birds and his encounter with the Queen of Sheba, who eventually comes before Solomon

TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r1.claim: The queen's statement about kings entering a city prepares for her proposal to send a gift and wait to see what the messengers report back.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r1.anchor: فقوله { إن الملوك إذا دخلوا } الخ، توطئة لقوله بعد { وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية فناظرة } الخ

TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r4.claim: The queen means to send a gift to Solomon, but avoids naming him, referring instead to him with his associates to portray royal power as acting through helpers, troops, and subjects.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r4.anchor: وهذا نوع من التجبر والاعتزاز الملوكي تصون لسانها عن اسمه وتنسب الأمر إليه وإلى من معه جميعا

TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r5.claim: The plural messengers shows a group carried the gift; Solomon's later command to return to them implies that the envoys had a leader.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#3/r5.anchor: ويعلم من قوله { المرسلون } أن الحامل للهدية كان جمعا من قومها كما يستفاد من قول سليمان بعد

TABATABAI:27:15-44#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:15-44#9/r1.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABATABAI:27:15-44#9/r1.claim: In al-Ihtijaj, the Commander of the Faithful explains that nāẓirah can mean waiting, citing the Queen’s words about waiting to see what the messengers return with.
TABATABAI:27:15-44#9/r1.anchor: وفي الاحتجاج عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام في حديث قال والناظرة في بعض اللغة هي المنتظرة ألم تسمع إلى قوله { فناظرة بم يرجع المرسلون }.

THALABI:v7p206/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p206/r3.claim: The author calls Belqis politically experienced and says she planned a gift to placate Solomon while testing whether he was a king.
THALABI:v7p206/r3.anchor: وذلك أن بلقيس كانت لبيبة قد سيست وساست، فقالت للملأ من قومها: إني مرسلة الى سليمان

THALABI:v7p206/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r4.speaker: بلقيس
THALABI:v7p206/r4.claim: Belqis reasons that a king would accept the gift and withdraw, whereas a prophet would refuse it and require them to follow his religion.
THALABI:v7p206/r4.anchor: فإن يكن ملكا قبل الهدية وانصرف، وإن يكن نبيا لم يقبل الهدية

THALABI:v7p206/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r5.speaker: بلقيس
THALABI:v7p206/r5.claim: Belqis sent Solomon a male and female attendant as part of the gift.

THALABI:v7p206/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p206/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says she dressed the male and female attendants alike so their sexes could not be distinguished.
THALABI:v7p206/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ألبستهم لباسا واحدا حتى لا يعرف ذكر من أنثى.

THALABI:v7p206/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r7.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p206/r7.claim: Mujahid says she dressed the boys as girls and the girls as boys.
THALABI:v7p206/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ألبس الغلمان لباس الجواري وألبس الجواري لبسة الغلمان

THALABI:v7p206/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r8.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v7p206/r8.claim: Miqatil gives the gift's attendants as one hundred boys and one hundred girls.
THALABI:v7p206/r8.anchor: فقال مقاتل: مائة وصيف ومائة وصيفة.

THALABI:v7p206/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r9.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p206/r9.claim: Mujahid gives the attendants' number as two hundred boys and two hundred girls.
THALABI:v7p206/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: مائتي غلام ومائتي جارية.

THALABI:v7p206/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r10.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v7p206/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi gives the attendants' number as ten boys and ten girls.
THALABI:v7p206/r10.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عشرة غلمان وعشر جواري.

THALABI:v7p206/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r11.speaker: وهب وغيره
THALABI:v7p206/r11.claim: Wahb and others give the attendants' number as five hundred boys and five hundred girls.
THALABI:v7p206/r11.anchor: وقال وهب وغيره: خمسمائة غلام وخمسمائة جارية.

THALABI:v7p206/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r12.speaker: ثابت البناني
THALABI:v7p206/r12.claim: Thabit al-Bunani reports that she sent gold plates in brocade containers; Solomon had jinn gild bricks and scatter them along the road, making the envoys' gift seem insignificant.
THALABI:v7p206/r12.anchor: عن ثابت البناني في قوله وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية قال: أهدت له صفائح ذهب في أوعية الديباج

THALABI:v7p206/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r13.speaker: قول غير مسمى
THALABI:v7p206/r13.claim: Another report says the gift consisted of four bricks of gold.
THALABI:v7p206/r13.anchor: وقيل: كانت أربع لبنات من ذهب.

THALABI:v7p206/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p206/r14.speaker: وهب وغيره من أهل الكتب
THALABI:v7p206/r14.claim: Wahb and other scriptural authorities describe five hundred cross-dressed attendants, ornate mounts and treasure, perfumes, and a box with an unpierced pearl and bent-hole bead, sent with tests of Solomon's knowledge.
THALABI:v7p206/r14.anchor: وقال وهب وغيره من أهل الكتب: عمدت بلقيس الى خمسمائة جارية وخمسمائة غلام فألبست الجواري لباس الغلمان

THALABI:v7p207/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p207/r1.speaker: بلقيس
THALABI:v7p207/r1.claim: Belqis instructed the boys to speak effeminately and the girls roughly, then told her envoy to judge Solomon: anger would suggest a king, while a gentle welcome would show a prophet.
THALABI:v7p207/r1.anchor: وأمرت بلقيس الغلمان فقالت: إذا كلمكم سليمان فكلموه بكلام فيه تأنيث وتخنيث

THALABI:v7p207/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p207/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p207/r2.claim: The hoopoe hurried to Solomon and informed him of the whole affair as the envoy carried the gifts.
THALABI:v7p207/r2.anchor: فانطلق الرسول بالهدايا وأقبل الهدهد مسرعا إلى سليمان (عليه السلام) فأخبره الخبر كله

RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r3.claim: The Qur’an gives no details about the gift, although people have speculated extensively about what it contained.
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r3.anchor: أما الكلام في صفة الهدية فالناس أكثروا فيها لكن لا ذكر لها في الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r4.claim: Her waiting to see what the messengers bring back shows she does not trust that the gift will be accepted and allows for refusal; she wants to discover Solomon’s aim.
RAZI-FULL:v24p168#2/r4.anchor: أنها لم تثق بالقبول وجوزت الرد

BURSEVI:v6p251/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p251/r1.claim: The queen says she will send envoys to Solomon and his people.
BURSEVI:v6p251/r1.anchor: {وإنى مرسلة إليهم} إلى سليمان وقومه رسلا {بهدية} عظيمة

BURSEVI:v6p251/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p251/r2.claim: A gift is an item offered with gentleness and courtesy.
BURSEVI:v6p251/r2.anchor: {بهدية} عظيمة وهي اسم للشيء المهدي بملاطفة ورفق.

BURSEVI:v6p251/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r3.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p251/r3.claim: Al-Mufradāt restricts hadiyya to a kindly gift exchanged from one person to another.
BURSEVI:v6p251/r3.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : الهدية مختصة باللطف الذي يهدى بعضنا إلى بعض

BURSEVI:v6p251/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r4.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v6p251/r4.claim: Kashf al-asrār explains nāẓira here to mean waiting.
BURSEVI:v6p251/r4.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : الناظر ههنا بمعنى المنتظر

BURSEVI:v6p251/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p251/r5.claim: Al-Kashifi’s Persian gloss likewise means waiting to see what happens.
BURSEVI:v6p251/r5.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (س نكرنده أم كه از آنجا)

BURSEVI:v6p251/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p251/r6.claim: Bima is originally bi-mā, an interrogative asking ‘with what?’ or ‘by what means?’
BURSEVI:v6p251/r6.anchor: {بم} أصله بما على أنه استفهام أي بأي شيء

BURSEVI:v6p251/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p251/r7.claim: The queen waits for the envoys’ answer so she can act according to the circumstances.
BURSEVI:v6p251/r7.anchor: بالجواب من عنده حتى أعمل بما يقتضيه الحال.

BURSEVI:v6p251/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r8.speaker: روي
BURSEVI:v6p251/r8.claim: The reported gift included five hundred boys dressed as girls, five hundred girls dressed as boys, lavish horses, a thousand gold and silver bricks, a jeweled crown, perfumes, an unpierced pearl, and a crookedly bored carnelian bead.
BURSEVI:v6p251/r8.anchor: روي : أنها بعثت خمسمائة غلام عليهم ثياب الجواري وحليهن كالأساور والأطواق

BURSEVI:v6p251/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r9.speaker: روي
BURSEVI:v6p251/r9.claim: She sent the gift with al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr and wise notables, testing whether Solomon could identify disguised sexes, describe a hidden case, and thread the pearl; she also watched his reaction.
BURSEVI:v6p251/r9.anchor: وضمت إليه رجالا من قومها ذوي رأي وعقل وقالت : إن كان نبيا ميز بين الغلمان والجواري

BURSEVI:v6p251/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r10.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v6p251/r10.claim: The Mathnawī characterizes Bilqīs’s gift as a load consisting entirely of gold bricks.
BURSEVI:v6p251/r10.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : هديه بلقيس هل اشتر بدست بار آنها جمله خشت زر بدست

BURSEVI:v6p251/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p251/r11.speaker: روي
BURSEVI:v6p251/r11.claim: After the hoopoe informed Solomon, he had jinn pave a six-farsakh field with gold and silver, build decorated walls, arrange fine land and sea animals and many jinn children, then sat on his throne among chairs.
BURSEVI:v6p251/r11.anchor: فأمر سليمان الجن فضربوا لبن الذهب والفضة وفرشوها في ميدان بين يديه طوله ستة فراسخ

STUDYQURAN:27:35/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:35/r1.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:27:35/r1.claim: Commentators give sometimes lengthy descriptions of the gifts, though the source of such details is unclear.
STUDYQURAN:27:35/r1.anchor: The commentators give details to the story, describing—sometimes at length—what the gifts were

STUDYQURAN:27:35/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:35/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:27:35/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī dismisses those gift details as irrelevant to the story.
STUDYQURAN:27:35/r2.anchor: commentators such as al-Rāzī dismiss such details as irrelevant to the story

TAB-FULL:v18p52/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r1.claim: The queen sends a gift to test whether Solomon is a king or a prophet: a prophet would refuse it and require them to follow his religion, while a king would accept it and withdraw.
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r1.anchor: قالت: إن يكن نبيا لم يقبل الهدية، ولم يرضه منا إلا أن نتبعه على دينه

TAB-FULL:v18p52/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the queen sent male and female attendants dressed alike; if Solomon distinguished them and returned the gift, she would leave her kingdom, follow his faith, and join him.
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قالت: " {وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية فناظرة بم يرجع المرسلون} [النمل: 35] قال: وبعثت إليه بوصائف ووصفاء

TAB-FULL:v18p52/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r3.claim: Mujāhid says she dressed the girls as boys and the boys as girls.
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: " {وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية} [النمل: 35] قال: بجوار لباسهم لباس الغلمان، وغلمان لباسهم لباس الجواري

TAB-FULL:v18p52/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj specifies that the gift included two hundred boys and two hundred girls.
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قولها: " {وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية} [النمل: 35] قال: مائتي غلام ومائتي جارية

TAB-FULL:v18p52/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r5.claim: Mujāhid says Solomon separated the boys from the girls and refused the gift, proving to the queen that he was a prophet she should follow.
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r5.anchor: قال ابن جريج، قال مجاهد: «فخلص سليمان بعضهم من بعض، ولم يقبل هديتها»

TAB-FULL:v18p52/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r6.speaker: ثابت البناني
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r6.claim: Thābit al-Bunānī says she sent gold plates in brocade containers; Solomon had the jinn gild bricks and scatter them on the road, making her envoys think little of their own gift.
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r6.anchor: عن ثابت البناني، قال: «أهدت له صفائح الذهب في أوعية الديباج؛ فلما بلغ ذلك سليمان أمر الجن فموهوا له الآجر بالذهب، ثم أمر به فألقي في الطرق؛

TAB-FULL:v18p52/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the queen thought that if Solomon wanted worldly goods they could satisfy him, but if he wanted religion he would accept no alternative to it.
TAB-FULL:v18p52/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {إن الملوك إذا دخلوا قرية أفسدوها} [النمل: 34] . . الآية، وقالت: إن هذا الرجل إن كان إنما همته الدنيا فسنرضيه، وإن كان إنما يريد الدين فلن يقبل غيره

TAB-FULL:v18p55/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p55/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v18p55/r1.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih portrays Bilqīs as an intelligent, politically experienced ruler whose people followed a zindīq religion; after receiving Solomon's unusual letter she consulted Yemen's chiefs, weighed the danger of a prophet against a rival king, and sent royal gifts to test whether he sought wealth or conversion to his faith.
TAB-FULL:v18p55/r1.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، قال: " كانت بلقيس امرأة لبيبة أديبة في بيت ملك، لم تملك إلا لبقايا من مضى من أهلها، إنه قد سيست وساست

TAB-FULL:v18p56/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p56/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v18p56/r1.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says she sent a gold ingot, reasoning that its response would show whether Solomon wanted worldly life or the hereafter.
TAB-FULL:v18p56/r1.anchor: عن أبي صالح: " {وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية} [النمل: 35] قال: أرسلت بلبنة من ذهب، وقالت: إن كان يريد الدنيا علمته، وإن كان يريد الآخرة علمته

TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r1.claim: Although the gift was sent to Solomon alone, the plural destination is idiomatic, as in the previously explained expression about Pharaoh and his chiefs.
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r1.anchor: وقالت: {وإني مرسلة إليهم} [النمل: 35] وإنما أرسلت إلى سليمان وحده على النحو الذي بينا في قوله: {على خوف من فرعون وملئهم} [يونس: 83]

TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r2.claim: The alif of mā is dropped in bimā because interrogative mā attached to a preposition loses its alif, distinguishing it from noninterrogative mā; the author cites 78:1 and 4:97.
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r2.anchor: بمعنى أي، ثم وصلوها بحرف خافض أسقطوا ألفها تفريقا بين الاستفهام وغيره، كما قال جل ثناؤه {عم يتساءلون} [النبأ: 1]

TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r3.claim: A cited wāfir verse retains the alif in ʿalā mā, showing that poets sometimes preserve it in this construction.
TAB-FULL:v18p56#2/r3.anchor: وربما أثبتوا فيها الألف، كما قال الشاعر: [البحر الوافر] علاما قام يشتمني لئيم … كخنزير تمرغ في تراب

TABRISI:27:32-35/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-35/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:32-35/r4.claim: In فلما جاء سليمان, the implicit subject of جاء refers to the omitted object of مرسلة; the understood wording is إني مرسلة رسولا.
TABRISI:27:32-35/r4.anchor: فلما جاء سليمان فاعل جاء الضمير المستكن فيه الراجع إلى مفعول مرسلة المحذوف لأن تقديره إني مرسلة رسولا

TABRISI:27:32-35/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-35/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:32-35/r14.claim: She will send a gift to placate Suleiman's rule and wait for the messengers to return with acceptance or rejection.
TABRISI:27:32-35/r14.anchor: فناظرة } أي فمنتظرة { بم يرجع المرسلون } بقبول أم رد

TABRISI:27:32-35/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-35/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:32-35/r15.claim: She knows kings value gifts and uses this exchange to test whether Suleiman is a king or prophet: acceptance means king, refusal prophet.
TABRISI:27:32-35/r15.anchor: لأنها عرفت عادة الملوك في حسن موقع الهدايا عندهم وكان غرضها أن يتبين لها بذلك أنه ملك أو نبي

TABRISI:27:32-35/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-35/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:27:32-35/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas says she sent male and female attendants dressed alike so their sexes could not be distinguished.
TABRISI:27:32-35/r16.anchor: أهدت إليه وصفاء ووصايف ألبستهم لباسا واحدا حتى لا يعرف ذكر من أنثى عن ابن عباس.

TABRISI:27:32-35/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-35/r17.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:27:32-35/r17.claim: Mujahid says she sent two hundred boys and two hundred girls, dressing the boys as girls and the girls as boys.
TABRISI:27:32-35/r17.anchor: أهدت مائتي غلام ومائتي جارية ألبست الغلمان لباس الجواري وألبست الجواري ألبسة الغلمان عن مجاهد.

TABRISI:27:32-35/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-35/r18.speaker: ثابت اليماني
TABRISI:27:32-35/r18.claim: Thabit al-Yamani says she sent gold plates in brocade containers; Suleiman plated bricks with gold and made the gift seem small.
TABRISI:27:32-35/r18.anchor: صغر في أعينهم ما جاؤوا به عن ثابت اليماني.

TABRISI:27:32-35/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-35/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:32-35/r19.claim: Another account lists five hundred cross-dressed boys and girls, jeweled clothes, five hundred mounts for each group, gold and silver bricks, a jeweled crown, an unpierced pearl, and a crookedly pierced bead.
TABRISI:27:32-35/r19.anchor: وقيل: إنها عمدت إلى خمسمائة غلام وخمسمائة جارية فألبست الجواري الأقبية والمناطق

TABRISI:27:32-37/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-37/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:32-37/r1.claim: In this gift account, she sends the noble al-Mundhir ibn Amr with advisers and a letter challenging Suleiman to identify the sexes, describe the box's contents, bore a pearl straight, and thread a bent bead without human or jinn help; an angry look marks a king, a kind look a prophet.
TABRISI:27:32-37/r1.anchor: ودعت رجلا من أشراف قومها اسمه المنذر بن عمرو وضمت إليه رجالا من قومها أصحاب رأي وعقل

TABRISI:27:32-37/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-37/r2.speaker: وهب وغيره
TABRISI:27:32-37/r2.claim: Wahb and others report that Suleiman had the jinn pave a long approach with gold and silver bricks, arrange ranks of jinn, demons, humans, animals, and birds, and sit before thousands of chairs; the envoys humbled themselves and cast down gifts.
TABRISI:27:32-37/r2.anchor: هذا كله مروي عن وهب وغيره.

TABRISI:27:32-37/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-37/r3.speaker: وهب وغيره
TABRISI:27:32-37/r3.claim: Gabriel tells Suleiman the box contains an unpierced pearl and a crookedly pierced bead; the envoy confirms his answer, and a termite bores the pearl while a white worm threads the bead.
TABRISI:27:32-37/r3.anchor: هذا كله مروي عن وهب وغيره.

TABRISI:27:32-37/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:32-37/r4.speaker: وهب وغيره
TABRISI:27:32-37/r4.claim: The report says girls transfer water between hands and wash their faces, pour over the inner forearm, and pour steadily; boys take water straight to the face, use the outer forearm, and dash it onto the hand.
TABRISI:27:32-37/r4.anchor: هذا كله مروي عن وهب وغيره.

TABRISI:27:36-37/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:36-37/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:36-37/r1.claim: Another account says she sent an inherited staff of the Himyarite kings and asked Suleiman to distinguish its top from bottom, plus a cup of water neither from earth nor heaven; he suspends the staff and fills the cup with horse sweat.
TABRISI:27:36-37/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنها أنفذت مع هداياها عصا كان يتوارثها ملوك حمير وقالت أريد أن تعرفني رأسها من أسفلها وبقدح ماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r1.claim: The queen says she will placate them regarding her kingdom if they are people concerned with worldly gain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: أصانعهم على ملكي إن كانوا أهل دنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r2.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the queen sent a gift to test Solomon and determine whether he was a king or a prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: تختبر بذلك سليمان وتعرفه أملك هو أم نبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say the gift included one hundred male attendants and one hundred female attendants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أرسلت إليهم بمائة وصيف ومائة وصيفة. وهو قول مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r4.claim: Mujahid gives the number as two hundred boys and two hundred girls; most exegetes agree the gift was boys and girls but differ on their numbers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: مائتي غلام، ومائتي جارية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r5.speaker: ثابت البناني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r5.claim: Thabit al-Bunani says she sent gold plates in brocade vessels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r5.anchor: وقال ثابت البناني: أهدت له صفائح الذهب في أوعية الديباج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r6.claim: She waits to see whether the envoys return from Solomon with acceptance or rejection of the gift.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r7.claim: Al-Farra’ explains that the alif in interrogative ما drops after a preposition when it means أي, distinguishing a question from a statement; retaining it is also correct.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r7.anchor: قال الفراء: انقصت الألف من (بم)؛ لأنها في معنى: بأي شيء، وإذا كانت (ما) في موضع: أي، ثم وصلت بحرف خافض نقصت الألف من (ما)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj says a preposition and interrogative ما function as one unit, so the alif drops to distinguish interrogation from a declarative phrase.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج: حروف الجر مع (ما) في الاستفهام تحذف معها الألف من (ما)؛ لأنهما كالشيء الواحد، وليفصل بين الخبر والاستفهام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r9.speaker: المفضل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r9.claim: Al-Farra’ cites Mufaddal’s poetry to illustrate the interrogative construction and also cites a line retaining the alif in على ما.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r9.anchor: وأنشدني المفضل (¬3): إنا قتلنا بقتلانا سراتكم ... أهل اللواء ففيما يكثر القيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r10.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r10.claim: The queen chose the noble al-Mundhir ibn Amr and other discerning advisers, then sent them as an embassy with the gift.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p228/r10.anchor: دعت بلقيس رجلا من أشراف قومها يقال له: المنذر بن عمرو، وضمت إليه رجالا أصحاب رأي وعقل، وبعثتهم وفدا إلى سليمان مع الهدية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r1.claim: The Queen sends the gift to appease and test Solomon: a king would accept it, while a prophet would not.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r1.anchor: أصانعه بها وأختبره أملك هو أم نبي؟ فإن كان ملكا قبلها، وإن كان نبيا لم يقبلها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r2.claim: She waits to see what response her messengers bring back.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:35-38/r2.anchor: فناظرة بم } بأي شيء { يرجع المرسلون } من عنده

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r6.claim: The queen will judge by the messengers’ return: acceptance would show Solomon is a king, not a true prophet as he claims.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r6.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية فناظرة بم يرجع المرسلون} [النمل: 35] أي رسلي، إن قبل هديتنا فهو من الملوك، وليس من أهل النبوة كما ينتحل.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r7.claim: Qatāda reports that the queen sent a gold brick wrapped in silk and brocade to appease a worldly king; Solomon cast a gold brick under the animals’ feet, making her envoys’ gift seem small.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r7.anchor: سعيد عن قتادة: قال: قالت: {وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية} [النمل: 35] فمصانعتهم بها عن الملك إن كانوا أهل دنيا، فبعثت إليهم بلبنة من ذهب في حريرة وديباج.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r8.claim: In the same account, Solomon had a gold brick placed on the road under the animals’ feet, and the messengers saw it covered in their urine and dung.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r8.anchor: فبلغ ذلك سليمان، فأمر بلبنة من ذهب، فصيغت، ثم قذفت تحت أرجل الدواب على طريقهم، تبول عليها وتروث عليها،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid says she sent girls dressed as boys and boys dressed as girls; Solomon sorted them out and refused the gift.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p542#2/r9.anchor: وتفسير مجاهد أنها بعثت إليه بجوار قد ألبستهن لبسة الغلمان، وغلمان قد ألبستهن لبس الجواري، فخلص سليمان بعضهم من بعض، ولم يقبل هديتها.

QASHANI:27:35-36/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:35-36/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:35-36/r1.claim: The queen's gift represents sensory perceptions, psychic appetites, imagined and illusory pleasures, and material supports embellished by thoughts, impulses, and motives.
QASHANI:27:35-36/r1.anchor: من أموال المدركات الحسية والشهوات النفسية

QASHANI:27:35-36/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:35-36/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:35-36/r2.claim: The test is whether Solomon accepts the offer and inclines toward the self, or rejects it and becomes firmer in his inclination toward the Real.
QASHANI:27:35-36/r2.anchor: هل يقبلها فيلين ويميل إلى النفس أو يردها فيتصلب في الميل إلى الحق

ELMALILI:27:32-39#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:32-39#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:32-39#2/r7.claim: The queen sends a gift to probe Solomon’s character, see whether he can be appeased with wealth, and decide how to proceed.
ELMALILI:27:32-39#2/r7.anchor: Yani bu suretle huylarını yoklayacağım da ona göre hareket edeceğim. Bakalım mâl ü menâl ile savulabilecek kimseler mi?

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:32/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:32/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:32/r1.claim: The queen consulted her officials about Solomon’s letter; after hearing their account of military strength and leaving the decision to her, she favored peace because invasion would be disastrous, sent gifts, and awaited the envoys’ return.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:32/r1.anchor: Kraliçe, savaşın başarısızlıkla neticelenmesi durumunda düşman istilâsının kötü sonuçlarını anlatarak meseleyi barış yoluyla çözmenin daha uygun olacağını ifade etmiş

BAQILLANI:v1p164/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r1.claim: The line can be construed as recalling the day the speaker slaughtered his mount or as linked back to the day at Dārat Jaljal; Bāqillānī calls its first hemistich foolish.
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r1.anchor: تقديره اذكر يوم عقرت مطيتي أو يرده على قوله يوم بدارة جلجل وليس في المصراع الأول من هذا البيت إلا سفاهته

BAQILLANI:v1p164/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r2.speaker: بعض الأدباء
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r2.claim: An adab critic says the phrase ‘O wonder’ refers to the young speaker’s slaughtering his mount for the women; Bāqillānī rejects this as far-fetched and unsupported by the wording.
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r2.anchor: قال بعض الأدباء قوله يا عجبا يعجبهم من سفهه في شبابه من نحره لهن

BAQILLANI:v1p164/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r3.claim: Though critics praise the second hemistich’s simile, making ‘meat’ definite and ‘fat’ indefinite leaves unclear whether both describe the same animal and leaves one comparison undeveloped.
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r3.anchor: انه عرف اللحم ونكر الشحم فلا يعلم انه وصف شحمها وذكر تشبيه أحدهما

BAQILLANI:v1p164/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r4.claim: Praising the quality of food served to guests may be criticized, though Arabs traditionally boast of it while Persians regard such boasting as shameful.
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r4.anchor: وفيه شيء آخر من جهة المعنى وهو انه وصف طعامه الذي أطعم من أضاف بالجودة

BAQILLANI:v1p164/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r5.claim: Comparing fat to silk is a commonplace image rather than an original device; the added word ‘twisted’ mainly supplies the rhyme and is not regarded by artisans as badiʿ.
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r5.anchor: وأما تشبيه الشحم بالدمقس فشيء يقع للعامة ويجري على ألسنتهم فليس بشيء قد سبق إليه

BAQILLANI:v1p164/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r6.claim: Boasting about food given to loved ones is blameworthy, unlike permissible pride in feeding guests, unless the speaker uses joking or playful manner.
BAQILLANI:v1p164/r6.anchor: أن تبجحه بما أطعم للأحباب مذموم وإن سوغ التبجح بما أطعم للأضياف

BURHAN:v2p236/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p236/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p236/r11.claim: Some take the plural messengers in Bilqis's speech to mean one envoy, supported by the singular command return to them; the author objects that the address could be to a leader, since kings commonly send groups.

BURHAN:v3p6#3/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p6#3/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v3p6#3/r3.claim: Ibn Faris takes the plural 'the messengers' as a single envoy, supported by the singular command 'Return to them.'
BURHAN:v3p6#3/r3.anchor: ابن فارس قوله تعالى ﴿ وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية

BURHAN:v3p6#3/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p6#3/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p6#3/r4.claim: The author objects that the queen may address her chief, and that royal custom often sends more than one messenger.
BURHAN:v3p6#3/r4.anchor: وفيه نظر من جهة أنه يحتمل مخاطبة رئيسهم فإن العادة جارية لا سيما من الملوك

ITQAN:v3p104/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p104/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v3p104/r2.claim: Ibn Faris treats المرسلون as a plural for one messenger, supported by ارجع إليهم; al-Suyuti objects that the queen may address the chief of several envoys, as kings commonly send more than one.
ITQAN:v3p104/r2.anchor: وجعل منه ابن فارس ﴿ فناظرة بم يرجع المرسلون ﴾ والرسول واحد بدليل ﴿ ارجع إليهم ﴾ وفيه نظر لأنه يحتمل أنه خاطب رئيسهم

ITQAN:v2p529/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p529/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p529/r4.claim: In the queen’s question, the bāʾ is not attached to nāẓirah, as al-Ḥawfī says, because an interrogative has precedence; it attaches to the following verb.

DAMGHANI:v1p472/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r4.claim: Hadiyya means a gift or donation, and may also mean a bribe; the Queen of Sheba’s gift is the example.
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r4.anchor: الثاني الهدية بعينها العطية والرشوة قوله تعالى في سورة النمل وإني مرسلة اليهم بهدية

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r1.claim: نظر primarily means perceiving an object with sight; it can also be used figuratively when context signals that use.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r1.anchor: النظر : في الأصل : إدراك المنظور إليه بالعين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r2.claim: نظرت فلاناً can mean 'I waited for him'; أنظرته means delaying him, and النظرة is delay.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r2.anchor: ويقال : نظرت فلانا : بمعنى انتظرته . وأنظرته : أخرته والنظرة : التأخير .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r3.claim: نظير means an equal or counterpart, such that the two are alike when compared.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r3.anchor: والنظير : المثل . وهو الذي إذا نظر إليه وإلى نظيره كانا سواء .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r4.speaker: شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r4.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah lists sight as one of five uses of نظر.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r4.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : النظر يقال على وجوه : أحدها : الإدراك بحاسة البصر .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r5.speaker: شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r5.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah lists waiting as a use of نظر, matching the queen's waiting for the envoys' return.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r5.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : النظر يقال على وجوه :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r6.speaker: شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r6.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah also lists mercy as a use of نظر.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r6.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : النظر يقال على وجوه :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r7.speaker: شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r7.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah lists facing or being opposite as a use of نظر, as in one house facing another.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r7.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : النظر يقال على وجوه :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r8.speaker: شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r8.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah's fifth use is reflection on things to derive a judgement and thereby reach knowledge.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r8.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : النظر يقال على وجوه :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r10.claim: A Qur'anic sense is waiting; the queen waits to see what the envoys bring back.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p587/r10.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن النظر في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

FARRA:v2p292/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p292/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p292/r6.claim: The alif drops from mā when it means ayy shayʾ and joins a preposition, distinguishing an interrogative from a declarative; retaining it is also correct.
FARRA:v2p292/r6.anchor: نقصت الألف من قوله (بم) لأنها في معنى بأي شيء يرجع المرسلون

FARRA:v2p292/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p292/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p292/r7.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal transmits an unnamed poet's line retaining the alif in fīmā, an example of the permitted full form.
FARRA:v2p292/r7.anchor: وأنشدنى المفضل: إنا قتلنا بقتلانا سراتكم

FARRA:v2p292/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p292/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p292/r8.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal also transmits an unnamed poet's line with ʿalā mā, likewise illustrating retention of the alif.

FARRA:v2p292/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p292/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p292/r9.claim: The queen's “to them” refers to Solomon.
FARRA:v2p292/r9.anchor: وهي تعني سليمان كقوله (على خوف من فرعون وملائهم)

FARRA:v2p292/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p292/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p292/r10.claim: Although the envoy was reportedly one woman, the queen uses the plural for him; the next verse's singular means “when the messenger came to Solomon.”
FARRA:v2p292/r10.anchor: رسولها- فيما ذكروا- امرأة واحدة فجمعت وإنما هو رسول

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p173/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p173/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p173/r9.claim: The plural المرسلون refers to one envoy, as the next verse addresses him with singular ارجع إليهم.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p173/r9.anchor: وهو واحد، يدلك على ذلك قوله

NAHHAS:v3p210/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p210/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p210/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the queen sent a brick or ingot of gold; after seeing Solomon's gold walls, the envoys thought her gift small. Another account gives a different gift, though أتمدونني بمال supports gold.
NAHHAS:v3p210/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس أرسلت إليهم بلبنة من ذهب أو بذهب فرأت الرسل الحيطان من ذهب

NAHHAS:v3p210/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p210/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p210/r2.claim: The queen says she is sending the gift to them though it is for Solomon, using the royal convention of speaking of rulers through their people.
NAHHAS:v3p210/r2.anchor: وقالت مرسلة إليهم وإنما هو إلى سليمان صلى الله عليه وسلم كما يخبر عن الملوك

NAHHAS:v3p210/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p210/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p210/r3.claim: The expected بما loses alif before an interrogative; after a preposition, statements retain it, as in رغبت فيما عندك, while questions drop it, as in فيم نظرت.
NAHHAS:v3p210/r3.anchor: والأصل بما حذفت الألف فرقا بين الاستفهام والخبر وإنما يكون هذا إذا كان قبل ما حرف جر

NAHHAS:v3p210/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p210/r4.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p210/r4.claim: Al-Farra permits retaining the alif in the interrogative, which al-Nahhas calls irregular and contrary to the Qur'anic form.
NAHHAS:v3p210/r4.anchor: وأجاز الفراء إثباتها في الاستفهام وهذا من الشذوذ التي جاء القرآن بخلافها

SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r1.claim: Hadiyya is something sent as a courtesy and names the gifted object; it could historically be a passive-participle noun, but is not a regular verbal noun of the form-four verb ahdā, whose masdar is ihdāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r1.anchor: والهدية: ما بعث على جهة الإكرام، وهي اسم للمهدى

SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r2.claim: Fa-nāẓiratun coordinates with mursilatun; bi-ma is governed by yarjiʿu, with the interrogative fronted and the question suspending nāẓira.
SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r2.anchor: عطف على " مرسلة ". و " بم " متعلق ب " يرجع "

SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r3.speaker: الهوفي
SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r3.claim: Al-Ḥawfī mistakenly attaches bi-ma to nāẓira; the author says that fails because the interrogative must lead its clause.
SAMIN-DURR:27:35/r3.anchor: وقد وهم الحوفي فجعلها متعلقة ب " ناظرة " وهذا لا يستقيم

ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r3.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r3.claim: Exegetical reports say the queen sent a gold brick, or gold bricks, wrapped in silk.
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r3.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنها أهدت سليمان لبنة ذهب

ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r4.claim: One account says Solomon put a gold brick where animals urinated and defecated, making the visitors' gift seem small.
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r4.anchor: فأمر سليمان بلبنة ذهب فطرحت تحت الدواب

ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r5.claim: Although other gift accounts are reported, Solomon's question about wealth indicates the gift was money.
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r5.anchor: مما يدل على أن الهدية كانت مالا

ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p119/r6.claim: After a preposition, interrogative ما loses its alif to distinguish a question; non-interrogative ما keeps it.

NASHR:v1p316/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p316/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
NASHR:v1p316/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd objected that the recitation was not what the Prophet taught him and cited إنما الصدقات للفقراء والمساكين as the form to prolong.
NASHR:v1p316/r1.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود: ما هكذا أقرأنيها رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

NASHR:v1p316/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p316/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p316/r2.claim: The author calls the report a clear proof for this topic, says its transmitters are trustworthy, and attributes it to al-Ṭabarānī’s al-Muʿjam al-kabīr.
NASHR:v1p316/r2.anchor: هذا حديث جليل حجة ونص في هذا الباب، رجال إسناده ثقات.

NASHR:v1p316/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p316/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p316/r3.claim: Other authorities relate the degrees of madd here to their degrees for separate madd, while disputing how many ranks there are.
NASHR:v1p316/r3.anchor: وذهب الآخرون مع من قدمنا ذكره آنفا إلى تفاضل مراتب المد فيه

NASHR:v1p316/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p316/r4.speaker: طاهر بن غلبون والداني وابن بليمة وابن الباذش
NASHR:v1p316/r4.claim: These authorities and others count four ranks: fullest, then three successively shorter ranks, with the last being omission of incidental lengthening.
NASHR:v1p316/r4.anchor: فذهب أبو الحسن طاهر بن غلبون، والحافظ أبو عمرو الداني وأبو علي الحسن

NASHR:v1p316/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p316/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p316/r5.claim: Although al-Taysīr may appear to imply another rank, the author rejects that inference and says its transmission supports only four.
NASHR:v1p316/r5.anchor: وليس ذلك بصحيح، بل لا يصح أن يؤخذ من طرقه إلا بأربع مراتب

NASHR:v1p316/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p316/r6.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p316/r6.claim: Al-Dānī’s account gives Sūsī and Ibn Kathīr short separate madd but medium connected madd, and says Dūrī and Qālūn consistently use medium connected madd.
NASHR:v1p316/r6.anchor: إنه قرأ للسوسي وابن كثير بقصر المنفصل وبمد متوسط في المتصل،

NASHR:v1p316/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p316/r7.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p316/r7.claim: Al-Dānī’s Jāmiʿ adds a fifth, longer rank for specified routes that pause before the hamza; the author explains it as the length of the pause with fully prolonged madd.
NASHR:v1p316/r7.anchor: وزاد في المتصل والمنفصل جميعا مرتبة خامسة، هي أطول من الأولى

NASHR:v1p316/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p316/r8.speaker: ابن مهران وابن الفحام والأهوازي والعراقي وابنه وابن الفخر الجاجاني
NASHR:v1p316/r8.claim: This group counts three ranks of madd; the excerpt begins its list with the middle rank and one above it.
NASHR:v1p316/r8.anchor: وذهب الإمام أبو بكر بن مهران في البسيط، وأبو القاسم بن الفحام،

QIRAAT-ER:27:35:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:35:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:35:9#1/r1.claim: A pausal hāʾ is added after interrogative mā; it marks a pause without changing meaning and confirms that mā is interrogative, not relative.
QIRAAT-ER:27:35:9#1/r1.anchor: Pausal hāʾ added to mā after bāʾ — bimah vs bima; hāʾ al-sakt marks pause

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#3/r1.speaker: ثابت البناني
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#3/r1.claim: Thābit al-Bunānī reports that the queen sent gold plates in brocade containers; Solomon spread gold-coated bricks along the road, making her envoys judge their gift worthless beside what lay everywhere.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81#3/r1.anchor: عن ثابت البناني في قوله تعالى ﴿ وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية ﴾ قال أهدت له صفائح الذهب في أوعية الديباج فلما بلغ ذلك سليمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r1.claim: Kings customarily accept gifts, signaling approval and affection; the Queen sends envoys with a gift to Solomon and his entourage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r1.anchor: ولما كانت عادة الملوك قبول الهدايا، وأن قبولها يدل على الرضا والألفة، قالت: وإني مرسلة إليهم، أي إلى سليمان ومن معه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r2.claim: She leaves the gift unspecified; accounts identifying it, her stratagems, and Solomon's reaction are contradictory and unreliable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r2.anchor: وجاء لفظ الهدية مبهما. وقد ذكروا في تعيينها أقوالا مضطربة متعارضة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r3.claim: Fanāẓiratun coordinates with mursalatun and bi-ma attaches to يرجع; the clause is suspended as the object of waiting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r3.anchor: والنظر هنا معلق أيضا. والجملة في موضع مفعول به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r4.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r4.claim: Al-Ḥawfī attaches bi to nāẓira; Abū Ḥayyān calls this a gross error.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r4.anchor: ووقع للحوفي أن الباء متعلقة بناظرة، وهو وهم فاحش،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r5.claim: Her wording shows she was unsure Solomon would accept the gift and considered refusal; she wanted his response to reveal his purpose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r5.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أنها لم تثق بقبول الهدية، بل جوزت الرد، وأرادت بذلك أن ينكشف لها غرض سليمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r6.claim: Al-hadiyya names a thing given, just as al-ʿaṭiyya names a thing bestowed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r6.anchor: والهدية: اسم لما يهدى، كالعطية هي اسم لما يعطى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r7.speaker: قالوا
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r7.claim: A report says she reasoned that a worldly king would accept wealth, whereas a prophet would reject it, so they should follow his religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r7.anchor: وروي أنها قالت لقومها: إن كان ملكا دنياويا، أرضاه المال وعملنا معه بحسب ذلك، وإن كان نبيا، لم يرضه المال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r8.claim: The speech omits “I sent the gift; when the messenger came to Solomon”; messenger is generic, and the term and pronouns can be singular or plural, masculine or feminine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r8.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره: فأرسلت الهدية، فلما جاء، أي الرسول سليمان، والمراد بالرسول الجنس لا حقيقة المفرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r9.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r9.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads جاءوا and ارجعوا, agreeing with the plural “envoys.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p236/r9.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: فلما جاءوا، وقرأ: ارجعوا، جعله عائدا على قوله: المرسلون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r1.claim: By proposing to send a gift and await the envoys, the queen settles on a course of action; this indicates she did not trust Solomon to accept it.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r1.anchor: حتى أعمل بما يقتضيه الحال وهذا ظاهر في أنها لم تثق بقبوله عليه السلام هديتها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r2.speaker: بلقيس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r2.claim: A report says she reasoned that a worldly king would be satisfied by wealth, whereas a prophet would not, and should be followed in his religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r2.anchor: وروي أنها قالت لقومها : إن كان ملكا دنيويا أرضاه المال

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r3.claim: Hadiyya names something offered as a gift, just as ʿaṭiyya names something given.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r3.anchor: والهدية اسم لما يهدي كالعطية اسم لما يعطى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r4.claim: Wa-nāẓira is coordinated with mursalatu; bi-ma depends on yarjiʿ, and the clause whose object is awaited is the complement of nazar.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r4.anchor: النظر معلق والجملة في موضع المفعول به له

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r5.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥawfī attached bi-ma to nāẓira, but al-Ālūsī calls this a grave error, following al-Baḥr.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r5.anchor: ووقع للحوفي أنه متعلق بناظرة وهو وهم فاحش كما في البحر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r6.claim: The verified nominal clause signals that she is firmly resolved to follow her judgment, unmoved by anything that might divert or dissuade her.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r6.anchor: والجملة الاسمية الدالة على الثبات المصدرة بحرف التحقيق

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the queen's gift consisted of one hundred male servants and one hundred female servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r7.anchor: فعن ابن عباس أنها كانت مائة وصيف ومائة وصيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r8.speaker: وهب وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r8.claim: Wahb and others describe five hundred girls dressed as boys and five hundred boys as girls, with jeweled mounts, gold and silver bricks, a jeweled crown, perfumes, and a box holding a pearl and a crooked-holed carnelian.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r8.anchor: وقال وهب وغيره : عمدت بلقيس إلى خمسمائة جارية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r9.speaker: وهب وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r9.claim: The queen sent a wise noble with tests: identify the disguised sexes and box contents, drill the pearl straight, thread the stone without human or jinn help, and watch whether Solomon appeared angry or welcoming.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r9.anchor: وقال وهب وغيره : عمدت بلقيس إلى خمسمائة جارية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r10.speaker: وهب وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r10.claim: On the envoys' approach, Solomon had a nine-farsakh gold-and-silver field prepared, assembled remarkable creatures and his subjects in ranks, and received the party with a welcoming face.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r10.anchor: وأمرهم بعمل ميدان مقدار تسع فراسخ

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r11.speaker: وهب وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r11.claim: Gabriel disclosed the box's pearl and stone; a termite bored the pearl and a white worm threaded the stone, each receiving trees or fruit as its provision, and Solomon distinguished boys from girls by how they washed.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r11.anchor: فجاء جبريل عليه السلام فأخبره بما فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r12.claim: Another account adds a hereditary Himyarite royal staff and a cup to be filled with water from neither earth nor sky; Solomon identified the staff's base by dropping it and filled the cup with horse sweat.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r12.anchor: وقيل : إنها أنفذت مع هداياها عصا كان يتوارثها ملوك حمير

ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r13.claim: Al-Ālūsī says these stories cannot be known to be true or false, though some details incline the heart toward judging them fabricated.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p198#2/r13.anchor: وكل ذلك أخبار لايدرى صحتها ولا كذبها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r1.claim: A hadiyya is a gift offered as a gesture of courtesy and affection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r1.anchor: والهدية هي: العطية على طريق الملاطفة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r2.claim: Baghawī portrays Bilqīs as intelligent and politically experienced.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r2.anchor: بلقيس كانت امرأة لبيبة قد سيست وساست

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r3.claim: Bilqīs meant to conciliate Sulaymān away from her kingdom and test whether he was a king or prophet: a king would accept and depart, while a prophet would refuse and require them to follow his religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r3.anchor: أي: إلى سليمان وقومه، بهدية أصانعه بها عن ملكي وأختبره بها أملك هو أم نبي؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the attendants wore identical clothes so no one could tell male from female.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس (2) ألبستهم لباسا واحدا كي لا يعرف ذكر من أنثى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the boys wore girls’ clothes and the girls wore boys’ clothes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ألبس الغلمان لباس الجواري وألبس الجواري لباس الغلمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives the retinue as one hundred male attendants and one hundred female attendants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r6.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: مائة وصيف ومائة وصيفة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid and Muqātil give the retinue as two hundred boys and two hundred girls.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r8.speaker: قتادة وسعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r8.claim: Qatāda and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say she sent a gold ingot wrapped in silk and brocade.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة، وسعيد بن جبير: أرسلت إليه بلبنة من ذهب في حرير وديباج

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r9.speaker: ثابت البناني
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r9.claim: Thābit al-Bunānī says the gift was gold plates in brocade containers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r9.anchor: وقال ثابت البناني: أهدت إليه صفائح من الذهب في أوعية الديباج

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r10.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r10.claim: Another account says the gift consisted of four gold ingots.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: كانت أربع لبنات من ذهب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r11.speaker: وهب وغيره
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r11.claim: Wahb and others describe five hundred cross-dressed boys and girls, adorned with gold and gems and mounted on five hundred mares and five hundred barādhīn; the gifts also included gold and silver ingots, a jeweled crown, perfumes, a pearl, and an agate bead.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r11.anchor: وقال وهب وغيره: عمدت بلقيس إلى خمسمائة غلام وخمسمائة جارية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r12.claim: Bilqīs sent the gifts with the noble al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr and advisers, and wrote prophetic tests: identify the attendants, disclose the box’s contents, drill a straight hole in the pearl, and thread the crooked bead unaided.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r12.anchor: ودعت رجلا من أشراف قومها يقال له المنذر بن عمرو، وضمت إليه، رجالا من قومها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r13.claim: She instructed the boys to speak effeminately like women and the girls to speak roughly like men when Sulaymān addressed them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p160#2/r13.anchor: وأمرت بلقيس الغلمان، فقالت: إذا كلمكم سليمان فكلموه بكلام تأنيث وتخنيث

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r1.claim: The queen explains her proposed reconciliation: she will send envoys bearing a gift to deflect Solomon from taking her kingdom.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r1.anchor: والمعنى إني مرسلة رسلا بهدية أدفعه بها عن ملكي

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r2.claim: She will assess Solomon's disposition from the envoys' return and then decide what to do.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r2.anchor: من حاله حتى أعمل بحسب ذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r3.claim: A report says she sent Minḏir b. ʿAmr with disguised boys and girls, a pearl and crooked bead as tests; informed by Gabriel, Solomon used worms and water to solve them, then returned the gift.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:35/r3.anchor: روي أنها بعثت منذر بن عمرو في وفد وأرسلت معهم غلمانا على زي الجواري وجواري على زي الغلمان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r6.claim: She chooses conciliation by sending a gift to the king and his soldiers, intended as a courteous overture.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r6.anchor: اي إليه وإلى جنوده { بهدية } أي تقع منهم موقعا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r7.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r7.claim: Al-Baghawī defines the gift as a present offered as a friendly overture.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r7.anchor: قال البغوي : وهي العطية على طريق الملاطفة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r8.claim: She will assess what the messengers bring back in words or appearance, then decide what to do, avoiding a premature confrontation.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r9.claim: An account says the gift included 500 boys dressed as girls and instructed to speak as girls, and 500 girls dressed as boys and instructed to speak as boys, plus a crooked gem and an unpierced pearl.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r9.anchor: خمسمائة غلام مرد , زينتهم بزي الجواري , وأمرتهم بتأنيث الكلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r10.claim: The queen asks Solomon to distinguish the boys from girls, pierce the pearl, and thread the crooked hole.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r10.anchor: وسألته أن يميز بين الغلمان والجواري , وأن يثقب الدرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r11.claim: The girl transfers water between her hands, slaps her face, and pours it inside her forearm; the boy throws water on his face and pours it over the back of his arm.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r11.anchor: فأمرهم بغسل الوجوه والأيدي , فكانت الجارية تأخذ الماء بإحدى يديها ثم تنقله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r12.claim: Solomon uses a termite to bore the pearl and a worm to pass a thread through the crooked hole.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p424/r12.anchor: وأمر الأرضة فثقبت الدرة , والدودة فأدخلت السلك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r1.claim: Qatada says the queen sent the gift to conciliate Solomon and test whether he and his people were worldly; she sent a gold brick wrapped in silk and brocade.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية قال : قالت اني باعثة اليهم بهدية فمصانعتهم بها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وأبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu Salih are said to give an account like Ibn Abbas’ report about the gift.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r2.anchor: وروى ، عن سعيد بن جبير وابي صالح نحو حديث ابن عباس .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r3.claim: Mujahid says the gift included servant girls dressed as boys and boys dressed as girls.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية قال : جواري لباسهن الغلمان ، وغلمان لباسهن الجواري .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says she sent eighty male and female servants with shaved heads as a test; Solomon distinguished them by their different ways of washing during ablution.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية قال : ارسلت اليهم ثمانين من وصيف ووصيفة ، وحلقت رؤوسهم كلهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r5.speaker: زهير بن محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r5.claim: Zuhayr reports her reasoning that a prophet would reject a gift and be impossible to fight, while a king would accept it; she sent eighty boys and two hundred girls, dressed and shaved to disguise their sex.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r5.anchor: ثنا زهير بن محمد في قول الله عز وجل : واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية فان يكن هذا الرجل نبيا لم يقبل هديتي ولا طاقة لكم بقتاله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r6.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r6.claim: Ikrima says the gift consisted of male and female attendants and a gold brick.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة قوله : واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية قال : الهدية وصفا ووصائف ولبنة من ذهب .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says she tested whether Solomon was a king or prophet by sending cross-dressed attendants, gold bricks, a pierced jewel, and a cup; Solomon exposed the disguises and had the city’s bricks gilded, making her envoys question the gift’s value.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2877/r7.anchor: عن السدي : واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية فناظره بم يرجع المرسلون وقالت : ان هو قبل الهدية فهو ملك فقاتلوه دون ملككم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r1.claim: In al-Suddi’s continuing account, the disguised attendants wash differently; Solomon threads a worm through the jewel and fills the cup with horse sweat, and the queen had intended to wage war.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r1.anchor: اما الجارية فافرغت على يدها ، واما الغلام فاغترف وقالوا ادخل لنا في هذه الخرزة خيطا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the gift was jewelry.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله : واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية قال : كانت الهدية جوهرا .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r3.claim: Qatada reports that Solomon distinguished boys and girls by their different ablution washing: boys washed the outer forearms first, girls the inner forearms.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ان الهدية هذه لما جاءت سليمان ميز بين الغلمان والجواري وفضهم بالوضوء

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r4.speaker: ثابت البناني
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r4.claim: Thabit al-Bunani says the queen sent gold plates in brocade containers; Solomon had the jinn gild bricks and scatter them along the road, so her envoys saw their gift as paltry.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r4.anchor: عن ثابت البناني في قوله : واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية قال : اهدت له صحائف الذهب في اوعية الديباج

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r5.claim: Qatada praises the queen’s intelligence despite her idolatry, since she knew that gifts influence people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية قال : رحمها الله ان كانت لعاقلة في اسلامها وشركها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says she sent the gift to test whether Solomon would accept it as a king or reject it as a prophet; his gilded palaces made the envoys wonder what use their gift could be.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2878/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس قال : فصارت حتى اذا كانت قريبة قالت : ارسل اليه بهدية فان قبلها فهو ملكا اقاتله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2879/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2879/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2879/r1.claim: Abu Salih says she sent a gold vessel or ingot as a test: if Solomon wanted wealth, she would know; Solomon replied by asking whether they offered him wealth.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2879/r1.anchor: عن أبي صالح واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية قال : اهدي له انية أو لبنة أو قال : انية من ذهب تجربه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2879/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2879/r2.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2879/r2.claim: Yazid ibn Ruman recounts that the queen judged the letter unlike any royal letter she had received: if its sender was a prophet, they could not resist and he sought their conversion; if merely a king, they could fight him, so she sent prized royal gifts to test his appetite for wealth.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2879/r2.anchor: عن يزيد بن رومان واني مرسلة اليهم بهدية فناظرة بم يرجع المرسلون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r1.claim: The queen's sentence introduces the decision she is about to announce and provides its rationale.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r1.anchor: مقدمة لما ستلقيه إليهم من عزمها ، ويتضمن تعليلا لما عزمت عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r2.claim: The bāʾ means accompaniment, and the omitted object of send is a letter and delegation accompanied by a gift, since an envoy would answer Solomon's letter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r2.anchor: باء المصاحبة . ومفعول { مرسلة } محذوف دل عليه وصف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r3.claim: Replying to a letter was an old custom and is treated as Muslim practice and a fellow Muslim's right; Ibn Ashur found no formal ruling in the legal schools.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r3.anchor: وهو من سنن المسلمين ، وعد من حق المسلم على المسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r4.speaker: القرطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi says a person who receives a letter with a greeting or similar content should reply, since a letter from an absent person resembles a greeting from someone present.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r4.anchor: قال القرطبي : إذا ورد على إنسان في كتاب بالتحية أو نحوها ينبغي أن يرد الجواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly considered replying to a letter obligatory, like returning a greeting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يرى رد الكتاب واجبا كرد السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur's apparent view is that a letter containing a greeting requires a written reply including a returned greeting, by analogy with spoken greetings; face-to-face silence more readily causes hostility.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن الجواب إن كان عن كتاب مشتمل على صيغة السلام أن يكون رد الجواب واجبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r7.claim: He says he found no reply in the Prophet's letters except his response to Musaylima, ending with peace upon whoever follows guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r7.anchor: ولم أر في كتب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جوابا عن كتاب إلا جوابه عن كتاب مسيلمة والسلام على من اتبع الهدى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r8.claim: A hadiyya is something offered to draw closeness and affection; hadaya is the standard plural, while the lower Madi dialect says hadawa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r8.anchor: فالهدية ما يعطى لقصد التقرب والتحبب ، والجمع هدايا على اللغة الفصحى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r9.claim: The plural hadaya derives from hadaʾi; speakers eased the heavy raised-case yāʾ and shifted the hamza between two alifs to yāʾ, while lower Madi shifts it to wāw.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r9.anchor: وأصل هدايا : هدائي بهمزة بعد ألف الجمع ثم ياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r10.claim: Nāẓira is the active participle of نظر meaning to wait or expect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r10.anchor: اسم فاعل من نظر بمعنى انتظر ، أي مترقبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r11.claim: The question either explains the queen's waiting or starts a new sentence; the order is changed to show uncertainty about what the envoys will bring back, with bāʾ before its object because interrogative mā takes clause-initial position.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p266/r11.anchor: فغير النظم لما أريد أنها مترددة فيما يرجع به المرسلون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r1.claim: Bilqīs reportedly planned to test Solomon with wealth and unusual things: a worldly king would be satisfied, but a prophet would persist in religion, so they should believe and follow him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r1.anchor: روي أن بلقيس قالت لقومها إني أجرب هذا الرجل بهدية أعطيه فيها نفائس الأموال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r2.claim: The author omits the gift’s many reported details because they are unreliable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r2.anchor: فبعثت إليه بهدية عظيمة أكثر بعض الناس في تفصيلها فرأيت اختصار ذلك لعدم صحته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r3.claim: Reported tests asked for water from neither earth nor sky, threading a twisted pearl without human or jinn, and piercing another; Solomon used horse sweat and a worm, while a termite pierced the pearl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r3.anchor: اختبرت علمه فيما روي بأن بعثت إليه قدحا فقالت املأه لي ماء ليس من الأرض ولا من السماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r8.claim: Mujāhid says Bilqīs also sent many enslaved boys and girls dressed alike to test Solomon’s ability to distinguish them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r8.anchor: وذكر مجاهد أنها بعثت في هديتها بعدد كثير من العبيد بين غلام وجارية وجعلت زيهم واحدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r9.claim: The author rejects this test as inadequate for so serious a matter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p259/r9.anchor: وليس هذا بتجربة في مثل هذا الأمر الخطير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the queen sent a gift to test whether Solomon was a prophet who rejected worldly wealth or a king who accepted it. She sent three gold bricks of a hundred ratls each, a pierced span-long ruby, and thirty boys and girls dressed alike; her letter challenged him to thread and seal the ruby and distinguish the attendants. Solomon had demons pave the road from his court for eight miles in each direction with gold bricks and ruby pillars. Envoys were impressed; he passed the thread through the ruby with an ant, sealed it, and returned it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس إنما أرسلت الهدية لتعلم أنه إن كان نبيا لم يرد الدنيا وإن كان ملكا فسيرضى بالحمل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r2.claim: Mujahid says Solomon swapped the boys' and girls' clothes to distinguish them and did not accept the queen's gift.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد جعلت لباس الغلمان للجواري ولباس الجواري للغلمان فميزهم ولم يقبل هديتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r3.speaker: وهب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r3.claim: Wahb says the gift included five hundred boys and five hundred girls.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r4.claim: Mujahid gives the attendants' number as two hundred boys and two hundred girls.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r4.anchor: والثالث مائتا غلام ومائتا جارية قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r5.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r5.claim: Ibn al-Sa'ib gives the number as ten boys and ten girls.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r5.anchor: والرابع عشرة غلمان وعشر جوار قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r6.claim: Muqatil gives the number as one hundred male and one hundred female attendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r6.anchor: والخامس مائة وصيف ومائة وصيفة قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r7.claim: One test had boys wash from elbow to hand and girls from hand to elbow so Solomon could distinguish them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p170/r7.anchor: أحدها أنه أمرهم بالوضوء فبدأ الغلام من مرفقه إلى كفه وبدأت الجارية من كفها إلى مرفقها فميزهم بذلك قاله سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r1.claim: Qatada says boys washed the backs of the forearms before the inner sides, while girls did the reverse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r1.anchor: والثاني أن الغلمان بدؤوا بغسل ظهور السواعد قبل بطونها والجواري على عكس ذلك قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says boys scooped water with their hands and girls poured water onto their hands.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r2.anchor: والثالث أن الغلام اغترف بيده والجارية أفرغت على يدها قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r3.speaker: التفسير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r3.claim: Another report says girls were told to speak to Solomon like men and boys like women.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r3.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أنها أمرت الجواري ان يكلمن سليمان بكلام الرجال وأمرت الرجال أن يكلموه كلام النساء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r4.speaker: التفسير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r4.claim: The queen sent a cup to be filled with water from neither sky nor earth; Solomon ran horses and filled it with their sweat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r4.anchor: وأرسلت قدحا تسأله أن يملأها ماء ليس من ماء السماء ولا من ماء الأرض فأجرى الخيل وملأه من عرقها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r5.claim: She waited to see whether the envoys returned with acceptance or rejection.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir says بما is the original form; when interrogative ما follows a preposition, its alif is dropped to distinguish it from declarative ما.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r6.anchor: قال ابن جرير وأصل بم بما وإنما أسقطت الألف لأن العرب إذا كانت ما بمعنى أي ثم وصلوها بحرف خافض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r7.claim: The pattern appears in عم يتساءلون and فيم كنتم; poetry may retain the alif, as in على ما قام يشتمنا.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p171/r7.anchor: كقوله عم يتساءلون النبأ وقالوا فيم كنتم النساء وربما أثبتوا فيها الألف كما قال الشاعر على ما قام يشتمنا لئيم كخنزير تمرغ في رماد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p189#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p189#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p189#2/r7.claim: The queen shifts to a truce and tactical appeasement, sending an appropriate gift to test Solomon; she hopes he may accept it, demand annual tribute, and spare them war.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p189#2/r7.anchor: ثم عدلت إلى المهادنة والمصالحة والمسالمة والمخادعة والمصانعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p189#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p189#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p189#2/r8.claim: Qatada praises the queen's good judgment both before and after accepting Islam, noting that she knew gifts influence people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p189#2/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: رحمها الله ورضي عنها، ما كان أعقلها في إسلامها وفي شركها!! علمت أن الهدية تقع موقعا من الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وغير واحد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and others report that the queen told her people: if Solomon accepts the gift, he is a king to fight; if he refuses it, he is a prophet to follow.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغير واحد: قالت لقومها: إن قبل الهدية فهو ملك فقاتلوه، وإن لم يقبلها فهو نبي فاتبعوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r1.speaker: غير واحد من المفسرين، من السلف وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r1.claim: Several early and later commentators say the queen sent a great gift of gold, jewels, pearls, and other valuables.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r1.anchor: ذكر غير واحد من المفسرين، من السلف وغيرهم: أنها بعثت إليه بهدية عظيمة من ذهب وجواهر ولآلئ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r2.claim: Some reports specify that she sent a brick of gold.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أرسلت بلبنة من ذهب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir considers the report that the queen sent golden vessels to be the sound view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r3.anchor: والصحيح أنها أرسلت [إليه] (1) بآنية من ذهب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وغيرهما
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r4.claim: Mujahid, Said ibn Jubayr, and others say the queen sent girls dressed as boys and boys dressed as girls, testing whether Solomon could identify them as a prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وغيرهما: وأرسلت جواري في زي الغلمان، وغلمان في زي الجواري، وقالت: إن عرف هؤلاء من هؤلاء فهو نبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r5.claim: One account says Solomon had the disguised youths perform ablution: the girl poured water over her hand while the boy scooped it, allowing him to tell them apart.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r5.anchor: فجعلت الجارية تفرغ على يدها من الماء، وجعل الغلام يغترف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r6.claim: Another version says the girl washed the inside of her hand before its back, while the boy did the reverse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: بل جعلت الجارية تغسل باطن (3) يدها قبل ظاهرها، والغلام بالعكس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r7.claim: A further version says the girls washed from their palms toward their elbows, and the boys from elbows toward palms.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: بل جعلت الجواري يغتسلن (4) من أكفهن إلى مرافقهن، والغلمان من مرافقهم إلى أكفهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r8.speaker: author
