IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir sees no contradiction among these different descriptions of how Solomon distinguished the disguised girls and boys.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r8.anchor: ولا منافاة بين ذلك كله، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r9.claim: Some say the gift included a cup to be filled with pure water from neither sky nor earth, and a bead and thread to test Solomon; he ran horses until they sweated, filled the cup with their sweat, and threaded the bead. Ibn Kathir says this is uncertain and mostly Israelite lore.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p190#2/r9.anchor: وذكر بعضهم: أنها أرسلت إليه بقدح ليملأه ماء رواء، لا من السماء ولا من الأرض، فأجرى الخيل حتى عرقت

JISHUMI:v8p5426/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5426/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5426/r12.claim: A gift and a grant are words of the same semantic class.

JISHUMI:v8p5426/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5426/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5426/r13.claim: Nāẓira means waiting; Arabs say “I looked for so-and-so” to mean “I awaited him.”
JISHUMI:v8p5426/r13.anchor: فناظرة: أي: منتظرة، تقول العرب: نظرت فلانا وأنا ناظره، أي: منتظره.

JISHUMI:v8p5426/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5426/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5426/r14.claim: Bima contracts from bimā by dropping the alif because it is interrogative, as in ʿamma yatasāʾalūn.
JISHUMI:v8p5426/r14.anchor: (بم) أصله بما، حذف الألف؛ لأنه استفهام، كقوله: (عم يتساءلون).

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r21.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the queen sent a gold ingot.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r21.anchor: أحدها : أنها كانت لبنة من ذهب , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r22.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r22.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the gift consisted of jewels.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r22.anchor: الثاني : أنها كانت جوهرا , قاله ابن جبير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r23.speaker: ثابت البناني
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r23.claim: Thabit al-Bunani says the gift was gold plates in brocade containers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r23.anchor: الثالث : أنها كانت صحائف الذهب في أوعية الديباج , قاله ثابت البناني .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r24.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r24.claim: Mujahid, ʿIkrima, Ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, and Zuhayr say she sent boys dressed as girls and girls dressed as boys.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r24.anchor: قاله مجاهد , وعكرمة وابن جبير , والسدي , وزهير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r25.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r25.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the group comprised eighty boys and girls in all.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r25.anchor: فقال سعيد بن جبير : كانوا ثمانين غلاما وجارية , وقال زهير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r26.speaker: زهير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r26.claim: Zuhayr says the group comprised eighty boys and eighty girls.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r26.anchor: وقال زهير كانوا ثمانين غلاما وثمانين جارية .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r27.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r27.claim: Qatada praises the queen's intelligence, saying she understood that a gift has influence on people whether they are believers or unbelievers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r27.anchor: قال قتادة : يرحمها الله إن كانت لعاقلة في إسلامها وشركها , قد علمت أن الهدية تقع موقعها من الناس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r28.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r28.claim: One account says she intended to soften Sulayman's attitude and induce him to yield.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r28.anchor: أحدهما : ما ذكره قتادة من الملاطفة والاستنزال .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r29.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r29.claim: Another account says she meant to test whether Sulayman was a prophet or a king.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r30.speaker: ابن عباس وزهير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r30.claim: In the test based on accepting or refusing the gift, acceptance would mark Sulayman as a king to be fought for his kingdom, while refusal would identify a prophet whom they could not fight.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r30.anchor: فقالت : إن قبل الهدية فهو ملك فقاتلوه على ملككم وإن لم يقبل الهدية فهو نبي لا طاقة لكم بقتاله , قاله ابن عباس وزهير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r31.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r31.claim: In one account of the test, Sulayman distinguished boys from girls by ordering ablution: boys scooped water with their hands, while girls poured it onto their hands.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r31.anchor: فاغترف الغلام بيده وأفرغت الجارية على يديها فميزهم بهذا ، قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r32.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r32.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r32.claim: Qatada's test has boys wash the backs of their forearms before the insides and girls wash the insides before the backs.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r33.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r33.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p207/r33.claim: Ibn Jubayr says boys began washing from elbow to palm, while girls began from palm to elbow.

MUQATIL:27:33-35/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r8.claim: The queen sends a gift to appease them over her kingdom if they are worldly people, then waits for the envoys’ answer.
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r8.anchor: { وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية } أصانعهم على ملكى إن كانوا أهل دنيا

MUQATIL:27:33-35/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r9.claim: The envoy leader was al-Mundhir ibn Amr; the gift included one hundred male and one hundred female servants dressed alike, plus two gems, one pierced and one unpierced.
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r9.anchor: المنذر بن عمر، والهدية مائة وصيف، ومائة وصيفة

MUQATIL:27:33-35/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r10.claim: The queen’s test was whether Sulayman could distinguish the boys and girls and tell the box’s contents: a prophet would do so and return the gift, while a king would accept it.
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r10.anchor: وقالت للوفد: إن كان نبيا، فسيميز بين الجوارى والغلمان ويخبر بما فى الحقة، ويرد الهدية فلا يقبلها

MUQATIL:27:33-35/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r11.claim: Sulayman distinguished the servants by their different hand positions while performing ablution: girls poured water over the forearm and boys over its back.
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r11.anchor: ميز بين الوصفاء والوصائف من قبل الوضوء، وذلك أنه أمرهم بالوضوء فكانت الجارية تصب الماء على بطن ساعدها

MUQATIL:27:33-35/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r12.claim: Gabriel informed Sulayman about the gems; a worm in soft silver pulled a thread through the crooked pierced gem, and a termite drilled the other without human or jinn help.
MUQATIL:27:33-35/r12.anchor: وكانت الجوهرة المثقوبة معوجة، فأتته دودة تكون فى الفضفضة وهي الرطبة

MUQATIL:27:36-37/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:36-37/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:36-37/r1.claim: The envoys asked for water neither from rain nor a spring; Sulayman ran horses until they sweated, strained the sweat into crystal cups, and impressed them. Gabriel told him the box’s contents; Sulayman disclosed them and returned the gift.
MUQATIL:27:36-37/r1.anchor: ماء لم ينزل من السماء ولم يخرج من الأرض، فأمر بالخيل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r1.claim: The queen says she will wait for the envoys' return.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r1.anchor: ﴿ فناظرة ﴾ فمنتظرة ﴿ بم ﴾ أي بما لأن الألف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r2.claim: Here بَم means بِما; the alif is deleted after a preposition in an interrogative.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r3.claim: She waits to see whether the envoys return with the gift accepted or rejected, knowing royal custom: a king accepts and departs, while a prophet rejects it and demands adherence to his religion.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r3.anchor: لأنها عرفت عادة الملوك وحسن مواقع الهدايا عندهم فان كان ملكا فبلها وانصرف وان كان نبيا ردها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r4.claim: The queen sent a lavish, elaborately dressed party of five hundred boys and five hundred girls, gold and silver bricks, a jeweled crown, a pearl, and a crooked-hole bead, led by al-Mundhir ibn Amr.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r4.anchor: فبعثت خمسمائة غلام عليهم ثياب الجواري وحليهن راكبي خيل مغشاة بالديباج

NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r5.claim: Her letter challenged Solomon, if he was a prophet, to distinguish the boys from girls, identify the container's contents, pierce the pearl, and thread the crooked bead; she told the leader to judge his reaction.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r5.anchor: وقالت فيه أن كنت نبيا فميز بين الوصفاء والوصائف وأخبر بما في الحق واثقب الدرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r6.claim: Solomon staged a grand display with gold and silver paving, animals, jinn, humans, and other creatures; the envoys threw down the gifts when they saw animals soil the precious paving.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r6.anchor: فأمر سليمان الجن فضربوا لبنات الذهب والفضة وفرشوها في ميدان بين يديه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r7.claim: Solomon smiled, solved the pearl and bead tests with an insect and a white worm carrying thread, tested the envoys with water to distinguish boys from girls, and returned the gift.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p211#6/r7.anchor: فأمر الأرضة فاخذت شعره ونفذت في الدرة وأخذت دودة بيضاء الخيط بفيها

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r1.claim: Bilqis wisely tests whether Solomon is a worldly king satisfied by wealth or a prophet who will refuse it and require faith and submission.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r1.anchor: هذا من حسن نظرها وتدبيرها أي إني أجرب هذا الرجل بهدية

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, reports that Bilqis sent Solomon a brick of gold; seeing his gold walls made the envoys' gift seem small.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r2.anchor: فقال سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس: أرسلت إليه بلبنة من ذهب

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r3.claim: Mujahid says Bilqis sent two hundred boys and two hundred girls.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أرسلت إليه بمائتي غلام ومائتي جارية

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas describes twelve girls disguised as boys, twelve boys as girls, musk and amber trays, gold-bearing mounts, two unusual beads, an empty cup, and a royal staff.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r4.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: باثنتي عشرة وصيفة مذكرين قد ألبستهم زي الغلمان

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r5.claim: One account says a single envoy carried the gift, accompanied by attendants and servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r5.anchor: وقيل: كان الرسول واحدا ولكن كان في صحبته أتباع وخدم

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r6.claim: Another account names the envoy as the noble al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr and says Bilqis sent one hundred boys and girls dressed in exchanged clothing, instructing them to speak in gender-disguised ways.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r6.anchor: وقيل: أرسلت رجلا من أشراف قومها يقال له المنذر بن عمرو

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r7.claim: In the same account, the hoopoe told Solomon about the envoy's clothing and speech; an alternative says God informed Solomon.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r7.anchor: فيقال: إن الهدهد جاء وأخبر سليمان بذلك كله. وقيل: إن الله أخبر سليمان بذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r8.claim: Solomon staged a vast display: gold and silver paving, exotic sea creatures, thousands of seats for prophets and scholars, and ranks of people, jinn, and animals; the envoys were awed and discarded their gifts.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r8.anchor: فأمر سليمان عليه السلام أن يبسط من موضعه إلى تسع فراسخ بلبنات الذهب والفضة

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r9.speaker: بعض الروايات
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r9.claim: A variant says Solomon left a gift-sized unpaved strip; the envoys dropped their presents there to avoid suspicion, then feared the demons but were escorted through the ranks.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r9.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات: إن سليمان لما أمرهم بفرش الميدان بلبنات الذهب والفضة

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r10.speaker: بلقيس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r10.claim: Bilqis told her messenger that an angry look would mark Solomon as a king, while a cheerful, gentle look would identify a prophet whose words he should understand and answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35/r10.anchor: وكانت قالت لرسولها: إن نظر إليك نظر مغضب فاعلم أنه ملك

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r1.speaker: بلقيس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r1.claim: Bilqis sent a gold box with an unpierced pearl and crookedly pierced bead, challenging Solomon to identify the attendants' sexes, box contents, staff ends, pierce and thread the objects, and fill a cup with dew.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r1.anchor: وكتبت كتابا مع رسولها تقول فيه: إن كنت نبيا فميز بين الوصفاء والوصائف

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r2.claim: When the envoy arrived, Gabriel informed Solomon what was inside the box, and Solomon told the envoy.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r2.anchor: فحركها، فأخبره جبريل بما فيها، ثم أخبرهم سليمان

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r3.claim: A termite carried a hair through the pearl's hole; Solomon granted its request to make its food come from trees.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r3.anchor: فجاءت الأرضة فأخذت شعرة في فيها حتى خرجت من الجانب الآخر

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r4.claim: A white worm threaded the crooked bead and asked Solomon to make fruit its food; he agreed.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r4.anchor: فقالت دودة بيضاء: أنا لها يا نبي الله فأخذت الدودة الخيط في فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r5.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says Solomon distinguished the boys and girls by their different ways of performing ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r5.anchor: قال السدي: أمرهم بالوضوء، فجعل الرجل يحدر الماء على اليد والرجل حدرا

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r6.claim: Other descriptions distinguish them by how they take water, which hand they use, and whether they wash the palm-side or back of the forearm.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: كانت الجارية تأخذ الماء من الآنية بإحدى يديها، ثم تحملها على الأخرى

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r7.speaker: يعلى بن مسلم عن سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Bilqis sent two hundred attendants; starting ablution at the elbow marked females and at the palm marked males, while a thrown staff revealed its base by whichever end reached ground first.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r7.anchor: وروى يعلى بن مسلم عن سعيد بن جبير قال: أرسلت بلقيس بمائتي وصيفة ووصيف

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r8.speaker: يعلى بن مسلم عن سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r8.claim: In that report, Solomon ran horses until they sweated, filled the cup with their sweat, returned the gift, and Bilqis concluded that this was a matter from heaven.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#2/r8.anchor: وأمر بالخيل فأجريت حتى عرقت وملأ القدح من عرقها، ثم رد سليمان الهدية

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r1.claim: The Prophet accepted and honored gifts but not charity; Solomon and the other prophets did likewise.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r1.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقبل الهدية ويثبت عليها ولا يقبل الصدقة

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r2.claim: Bilqis used acceptance as a test because Solomon demanded submission; a gift could not ransom that demand, and using it to buy truth would be forbidden bribery.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r2.anchor: وإنما هي رشوة وبيع الحق بالباطل، وهي الرشوة التي لا تحل

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r3.claim: A freely given gift for affection and connection is generally lawful, but the author qualifies this rule when the giver is a polytheist.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r3.anchor: وأما الهدية المطلقة للتحبب والتواصل فإنها جائزة من كل أحد وعلى كل حال

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r4.speaker: جماعة من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r4.claim: One hadith prohibits accepting polytheist support and gifts, while a report attributed to Malik from Thawr ibn Zayd says the Prophet accepted a gift; some scholars treated the reports as abrogating one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r4.anchor: في الحديث: " نهيت عن زبد المشركين " يعني رفدهم وعطاياهم

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r5.claim: The author prefers reconciling the reports: gifts are refused from those hoping to defeat the Muslims, take their land, or enter Islam by that means, as with Solomon's situation.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r5.anchor: وهذا أحسن تأويل للعلماء في هذا فإنه جمع بين الأحاديث

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r6.speaker: مالك عن عطاء بن عبد الله الخراساني
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r6.claim: A report attributed through Malik to ʿAta al-Khurasani says handshakes remove rancor and gifts create affection and remove hostility.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r6.anchor: روى مالك عن عطاء بن عبد الله الخراساني قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r7.speaker: معاوية بن الحكم
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r7.claim: Muʿawiya ibn al-Hakam says he heard the Prophet commend gift-giving as strengthening affection and removing inner rancor; al-Daraqutni calls its transmission singular and unreliable, and says it is not sound from Malik or al-Zuhri.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r7.anchor: وقال الدارقطني: تفرد به ابن بجير عن أبيه عن مالك، ولم يكن بالرضى

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r8.speaker: ابن شهاب
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r8.claim: Ibn Shihab reports that it reached him that the Prophet urged people to exchange gifts because gifts remove rancor.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r8.anchor: وعن ابن شهاب قال: بلغنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r9.speaker: آخرون
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r9.claim: Other scholars held that the conflicting reports do not involve abrogation.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#3/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون ليس فيها ناسخ ولا منسوخ

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r1.claim: A hadith says people sitting with someone share in a gift, and scholars differ over what that sharing means.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " جلساؤكم شركاؤكم في الهدية "

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r2.claim: One interpretation takes the companions' share literally; another treats sharing as generosity and good manners, without a right to compel the recipient.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r2.anchor: وقيل: يشاركهم على وجه الكرم والمروءة، فإن لم يفعل فلا يجبر عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r3.speaker: أبو يوسف
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r3.claim: Abu Yusuf limits the companions' share to fruit and similar foods.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r3.anchor: وقال أبو يوسف: ذلك في الفواكه ونحوها

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r4.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r4.claim: Some say companions share the happiness occasioned by the gift, not the gift itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هم شركاؤه في السرور لا في الهدية

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r5.claim: The report applies to groups such as the People of the Bench and residents of lodges or hospices; a scholar given a gift specifically is not required to share, though sharing is generous.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r5.anchor: أما إذا كان فقيها من الفقهاء اختص بها فلا شركة فيها لأصحابه

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r6.claim: Here فناظرة means waiting or expecting.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r6.anchor: أي منتظرة { بم يرجع المرسلون } قال قتادة: يرحمها الله

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r7.claim: Qatada praises Bilqis as discerning in both Islam and polytheism, since she knew gifts have an effect on people.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r7.anchor: قال قتادة: يرحمها الله أن كانت لعاقلة في إسلامها وشركها

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r8.claim: The alif is omitted in بما to distinguish it from declarative ما; retaining it is also permissible.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r8.anchor: وسقطت الألف في { بم } للفرق بين «ما» الخبرية. وقد يجوز إثباتها

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r9.claim: The cited line demonstrates the permissible written alif in على ما.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r9.anchor: على ما قام يشتمني لئيم كخنزير تمرغ في رماد

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r10.speaker: يونس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r10.claim: Yunus explains that السخيمة means rancor.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r10.anchor: قال ابن وهب: سألت يونس عن السخيمة ما هي فقال: الغل

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r11.speaker: عثمان الوقاصي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r11.claim: The route through ʿUthman al-Waqqasi from al-Zuhri is weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r11.anchor: وهذا الحديث وصله الوقاصي عثمان عن الزهري وهو ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r12.claim: The Prophet's acceptance of gifts is established and exemplary; gifts remove inner resentments and make encounters more gracious.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r12.anchor: وعلى الجملة: فقد ثبت أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقبل الهدية

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r13.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r13.claim: An unnamed poet says mutual gifts generate connection, affection, and pleasant social presence.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r13.anchor: هدايا الناس بعضهم لبعض تولد في قلوبهم الوصالا

QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r14.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r14.claim: A second unnamed poet says gifts are valued even more than a child by a fond parent.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:35#4/r14.anchor: إن الهدايا لها حظ إذا وردت أحظى من الابن عند الوالد الحدب
